subject: Cartwright Labs — Morning latency & error surge (prod)
messages:
From: Evan Cartwright <evan@cartwrightlabs.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <procurement@cartwrightlabs.com>
Date: 2027-07-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Cartwright Labs — Morning latency & error surge (prod)

Vanessa,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 5xx errors and tail latency across our checkout and recommendations endpoints this morning between ~08:50–10:10 PT. Error rate peaked at ~7% and p95 jumped from ~220ms to ~1.8s. Our customers are reporting sluggish behavior and a few timeouts.

I attached a short sampling of server-side logs and a monitoring snapshot. Can you confirm whether this is related to a model rollout or a capacity change on your side? We need an ETA for stabilization and any mitigation steps you can take immediately.

Attachments: [error-sample.log (text/plain)], [cartwright_monitoring_snapshot.png (image/png)]

Evan
Head of Ops, Cartwright Labs
E: evan@cartwrightlabs.com
T: +1 415 555 0182
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Evan Cartwright <evan@cartwrightlabs.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-28T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cartwright Labs — Morning latency & error surge (prod)

Evan — thanks for the heads up and the logs. I'm mobilizing a cross-functional response now.

Immediate actions:
- Stand up a short war-room (joining link below) for triage with SRE and infra.
- We'll run a short canary rollback if the recent model variant at 02:00 PT is implicated.
- We'll add temporary capacity (burst to dedicated pool) and enable stricter prefix caching for checkout RPCs.

I'll post rolling updates every 30 minutes until we hit stabilization. David (ops lead) and Marissa (SRE lead) are on this thread. Sean from CS will coordinate customer comms and credits.

War-room link: https://meet.redwood.com/warroom/WR-4451
PagerDuty: https://app.pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-987654

—V
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-28T09:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cartwright Labs — Morning latency & error surge (prod)

Joining the war-room now. Quick triage notes from my side:
- Confirm whether Cartwright is on the new 16k-context variant (model-tag: rwd/llamax-16k-v2) — that rollout targeted funded accounts this week.
- Need a short checklist: traffic shaping -> graceful fallback -> cache warm -> burst capacity -> monitor.
- Who's owning the customer-facing timeline and credit ask? (Sean)

Marissa — can you run a live diff of recent kernel selection logs and KV cache hit rates for cartwright namespace? If we can narrow to kernel mismatch or KV invalidation, rollback will be faster.

-David
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-28T09:50:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cartwright Labs — Morning latency & error surge (prod)

On Tue, 2027-07-28 at 09:32, David Kim wrote:
> Joining the war-room now. Quick triage notes from my side:

Triage summary (SRE):
- Observed increased tokenization costs for Checkout pipeline; model variant rwd/llamax-16k-v2 shows a small but consistent higher per-token latency for short prompts.
- KV cache hit rate for cartwright namespace dropped from 78% to 49% after a background cache flush at 08:45 PT (auto-maintenance window).
- Serving logs show an uptick in kernel fallback events on GPU nodes in us-west-2 between 08:48–09:12.

Immediate mitigations completed (09:48–09:58 PT):
1) Re-enabled pinned KV cache snapshots for cartwright namespace (cache restored; warming in progress).
2) Rolled back model routing for cartwright to rwd/llamax-8k-stable (targeted rollback completed at 09:52 PT).
3) Scoped burst capacity: +2 reserved GPU nodes to cartwright's dedicated pool (provisioned at 09:54 PT).
4) Enabled strict short-prompt fast-path to avoid tokenization regression for checkout calls.

Monitoring: p95 dropped from 1.8s -> 410ms within 12 minutes of rollback; 5xxs reduced from 7% -> 0.6%. Continued observation for 2 hours.

Next actions (owners):
- Marissa: keep incremental telemetry and GPU kernel logs open; schedule full kernel regression postmortem.
- David: coordinate follow-up meeting and executive readout in 2 hours.
- Sean: draft customer-facing note and settlement offer (credits) for Vanessa to review.
- Priyom: capture any contract/entitlement constraints if Cartwright requests extended credits.

Attaching: redwood_action_plan_v1.pdf (action summary).
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Evan Cartwright <evan@cartwrightlabs.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Priya Rao <procurement@cartwrightlabs.com>, Marco Leone <marco@azurepartners.com>
Date: 2027-07-28T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cartwright Labs — Morning latency & error surge (prod)

Evan — quick update from the war-room and our immediate commitments.

TL;DR: We identified a KV-cache invalidation during a maintenance window that, together with the recent 16k model variant, amplified tokenization latency for short-checkout calls. We executed a targeted rollback and capacity burst; metrics show large improvement.

What we did (summary):
- Rolled routing back to rwd/llamax-8k-stable at 09:52 PT.
- Restored pinned KV cache snapshots and accelerated warm-up.
- Provisioned +2 reserved GPU nodes in your dedicated pool for the next 6 hours to avoid cold starts.
- Activated fast-path for short prompts.

Observed impact: p95 improved to ~410ms and 5xxs down to 0.6% at 10:03 PT. We'll monitor for the next 4 hours and revert capacity after stabilization.

Next steps (48h plan):
- Root-cause analysis and timeline for kernel regression (Marissa to lead).
- Follow-up call with your engineering leads tomorrow 10:00 PT to review mitigations and longer-term hardening (David to schedule).
- Customer settlement: Sean will propose a one-time service credit (we're prepared to offer a partial month credit; exact amount to be confirmed once we sync with finance).

Links & artifacts: runbook and action plan: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-cartwright-runbooks
Incident ticket: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/ticket/HT-3321
PagerDuty: https://app.pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-987654

We're very sorry for the disruption — we know how consequential checkout latency is for Cartwright. I'll follow up with a formal incident readout and RCA draft within 48 hours. Please reply if you'd like immediate compensation details in this thread.

—Vanessa
From: Evan Cartwright <evan@cartwrightlabs.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <procurement@cartwrightlabs.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marco Leone <marco@azurepartners.com>
Date: 2027-07-29T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cartwright Labs — Morning latency & error surge (prod)

Vanessa / team — thank you for the rapid response and the detailed update. Metrics on our side look back to normal after the rollback and burst; conversions recovered within the hour.

A couple quick asks:
- Please share the RCA draft and kernel regression details as soon as available. We want the assurance this won't recur during next week's peak.
- We are open to the one-time credit you mentioned; Priya will follow up with Sean on the procurement side.

Appreciate the transparency and the fast mitigation — special thanks to Marissa and David for the quick roll.

Evan
